forward_spiral: Nash: count best structural shortcut, not brute-force candidate count
Goedel: charge discovery of a short proof separately from checking it
Edmonds: exact contraction can collapse an exponential-looking enumeration
Cook/Levin/Karp: one SAT key plus witness-preserving reductions is enough for universality
Schaefer: the right algebra/relations determine tractability on fixed languages
Yannakakis: compact lifted representation itself has extension-complexity debt
BGS: a universal proof must use nonrelativizing information somewhere
reverse_tranception: Assume a future universal JANUS transition exists.
Then its usefulness cannot come merely from reducing printed clause count; it must preserve semantics under future transitions.
Therefore the hidden object should be an operational congruence/extension, not a static compression.
If discovery of that congruence is itself hard, Goedel's discovery debt returns.
If its explicit representation or nested manipulation explodes, Yannakakis-style representation debt returns.
If it is limited to one fixed relation language, Schaefer escape returns.
If it only beats naive enumeration on one family, Nash's shortcut observation is satisfied locally but universality is absent.
Thus the next universal theorem target is operational closure of polynomially discoverable exact quotients/extensions under a single global resource bound.

new_central_target.name: POLYNOMIAL_EXACT_OPERATIONAL_CONGRUENCE_TOTALITY
new_central_target.statement: For every CNF F, there exists a uniformly polynomially discoverable exact representation B_F and certified transition algebra such that SAT/UNSAT semantics and witnesses are preserved, every admitted next operation remains within polynomial total representation/certificate/verification volume, and a well-founded proof-relevant potential makes polynomially bounded progress to decision.

demi_head_action: Implement only contract/adversary infrastructure now; do not implement a universal factorizer from this synthesis without a frozen independent holdout and exact grammar.
